open_points.subject: AuditEntry sequence minting after restore
open_points.text: “A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number”
open_points.question: What sequence number does the first new audit entry after restoration receive, and does “backup's last number” mean the highest number ever minted before that backup even when its entry had already been erased, or only the highest entry retained in the backup?
options: Restore the backed-up high-water number and mint the next number as high-water plus one
Use the highest audit entry still retained in the backup and mint one more
Reuse the backup's last number for the first new entry
open_points.default_guess: Restore the backed-up highest-ever-minted number and assign the first new entry that number plus one.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity across restored histories
open_points.text: “never reused within that history” and “the sequence number is what tells them apart”
open_points.question: When a restored history reuses numbers that existed only in the lost post-backup branch, is an AuditEntry identified only within its store history, and if so what identifies or supplies that history namespace?
options: AuditEntry identity is the pair of store-history identity and sequence number, with the history identity represented somehow
The sequence number identifies an entry only in the currently held history; histories have no represented identity and entries across them cannot be distinguished
Sequence numbers must remain unique across all pre-loss and post-restore histories
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sequence number as identity only within the currently held store history, without storing a separate history identifier.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure ownership and cardinality after restore
open_points.text: “it is a fact about the instance” and “Durable, at most one per instance” versus “present for the rest of the store's history” and “A store restored after a loss from a backup made before the import begins a history without it”
open_points.question: Is MigrationClosure scoped to the production instance or to one store history, and after a pre-import backup is restored and the import succeeds again, is the new closure the same logical value or a distinct history-scoped closure?
options: It is scoped to a store history; each restored history may independently acquire one closure
It is scoped to the instance; a repeated import recreates the same logical closure
It is scoped to the instance and the prior successful import must remain closed despite its closure being absent from the restored store
open_points.default_guess: Scope the closure to the current store history, allowing the restored history to acquire its own closure when the import is repeated.
